day.description: Computer use CLI for AI agents
day.readme: Computer use for AI agents: see and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree. agent-desktop gives an AI agent computer use without screenshots or pixel matching. It reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. The loop lives in your agent; agent-desktop has no model inside. It ships as a CLI and a C library.

day.description: Worktrunk is a CLI for Git worktree management, designed for parallel AI agent workflows
day.readme: Worktrunk is a CLI for git worktree management, designed for running AI agents in parallel. Worktrunk's three core commands make worktrees as easy as branches. Plus, Worktrunk has a bunch of quality-of-life features to simplify working with many parallel changes, including hooks to automate local workflows & copy-on-write build caches. AI agents like Claude Code and Codex can handle longer tasks without supervision, such that it's possible to manage 5-10+ in parallel.

day.readme: Tiny engine, immense model. colibri runs very large open models on the machine you already have. A mixture-of-experts model of hundreds of billions of parameters uses only a small part of itself for each token, so colibri keeps that part in RAM and reads the rest, the experts, from the disk when the model asks for them. Pure C, one file per model family, no GPU required. Thirteen engines run today.

day.description: Turn Claude Code into a full game dev studio, 49 AI agents, 72 workflow skills, and a complete coordination system mirroring real studio hierarchy.
day.readme: Turn a single Claude Code session into a full game development studio. 49 agents. 74 skills. One coordinated AI team. Building a game solo with AI is powerful, but a single chat session has no structure. No one stops you from hardcoding magic numbers, skipping design docs, or writing spaghetti code. There's no QA pass, no design review, no one asking "does this actually fit the game's vision?" Claude Code Game Studios solves this by giving your AI session the structure of a real studio.

Give it any website and it runs a full SEO audit in 10 to 15 minutes, then hands you a clear action plan, sorted by what matters most. It checks everything a good SEO consultant would: Technical SEO. Crawlability, indexing, sitemaps, robots.txt, redirects, page speed and Core Web Vitals. Content quality.

week.description: Vibe code with pi in a lightweight, real IDE that customises itself around the way you work, The Vibe You Need
week.readme: ThinkRail is the agentic IDE that gets better every time you use it, learning your project through living specs today, and building its own capabilities tomorrow. We built a rich interface around the pi coding agent, isolated work into separate workspaces, and gave the agent durable project knowledge through living specs and reusable skills. Next, we're adding full extension support, so ThinkRail can create the tools it needs based on how you actually work.

Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically to improve performance on specialized tasks. Skills teach Claude how to complete specific tasks in a repeatable way, whether that's creating documents with your company's brand guidelines, analyzing data using your organization's specific workflows, or automating personal tasks.

week.description: A collection of agent skills that help you build great interfaces.
week.readme: A collection of agent skills that cover UI, typography, colors, accessibility, layout, product writing and help you build a great interface. These skills cover topics that I write about on my personal website and my design engineering magazine, Interfaces. better-interface: Reviews a screen, flow or whole interface across accessibility, layout, writing, typography, color and UI polish, and returns one ranked report.

week.description: A single CLAUDE.md file to improve Claude Code behavior, derived from Andrej Karpathy's observations on LLM coding pitfalls.
week.readme: A single CLAUDE.md file to improve Claude Code behavior, derived from Andrej Karpathy's observations on LLM coding pitfalls. Four principles in one file that directly address these issues: Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs. LLMs often pick an interpretation silently and run with it.

week.description: 👻 Ghostty is a fast, feature-rich, and cross-platform terminal emulator that uses platform-native UI and GPU acceleration.
week.readme: Fast, native, feature-rich terminal emulator pushing modern features. A native GUI or embeddable library via libghostty . Ghostty is a terminal emulator that differentiates itself by being fast, feature-rich, and native. week.readme: Worktrunk is a CLI for git worktree management, designed for running AI agents in parallel. Worktrunk's three core commands make worktrees as easy as branches. month.description: Free, local plugin that keeps tool output out of your coding agent's context window. Sandbox and SQLite FTS5 search, 99% fewer bytes in context. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI and 4 more agents. Zero telemetry.
month.readme: The other half of the context problem. Every MCP tool call dumps raw data into your context window. A Playwright snapshot costs 56 KB. Twenty GitHub issues cost 59 KB. And when the agent compacts the conversation to free space, it forgets which files it was editing, what tasks are in progress, and what you last asked for.

new.description: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System
new.readme: dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for DeepSeek Harness. It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. new.description: Craft Anything: understand how any software works, and craft your own.
new.readme: See how any website, app or game works, then have AI build your own version; an open-source, clean-room engine in pure Rust. threats.title: MCP TypeScript SDK HTTP transports lack request limits
threats.headline: MCP TypeScript SDK servers over HTTP accepted unlimited bodies and batches, enabling unauthenticated denial of service
threats.summary: MCP servers built with the TypeScript SDK and reachable over HTTP put no limit on POST body size or on the number of messages in a JSON-RPC batch. Large requests could exhaust server memory, and one long batch could block the server from serving anyone else. No credentials were needed unless the application authenticates requests before they reach the SDK.
actions: Cap request body size in a reverse proxy until the SDK is upgraded.

action_quotes.action: Cap request body size in a reverse proxy until the SDK is upgraded.
action_quotes.quote: If you cannot upgrade yet, cap request body size in a reverse proxy.

who: MCP servers built on the TypeScript SDK
servers reachable over Streamable HTTP by untrusted clients
threats.quote: Large requests could exhaust the server's memory, and one long batch could block it from serving anyone else.

threats.title: vLLM image loader reaches Ghostscript on untrusted EPS input
threats.headline: vLLM passes untrusted image bytes to Pillow, enabling Ghostscript command execution on vulnerable hosts.
threats.summary: The same path also exposes a separate Pillow denial-of-service condition that can exhaust media-loading workers.
actions: Restrict who can reach image-capable vLLM endpoints.

action_quotes.action: Restrict who can reach image-capable vLLM endpoints.
action_quotes.quote: API-key authentication and network access controls determine who can reach the request path.

who: hosts with a vulnerable Ghostscript build
threats.quote: On a host with Ghostscript affected by CVE-2024-29510, this exposes the known Ghostscript sandbox escape through vLLM's image-loading path and can execute commands with the vLLM process's privileges.

threats.title: vLLM SHM multimodal cache allows forged handles to reach pickle
threats.headline: Authenticated vLLM callers can forge SHM cache handles to run arbitrary Python in worker processes.
threats.summary: When the SHM multimodal processor cache is enabled, vLLM treats an address and monotonic_id pair as authority to read shared memory in the worker. A caller can forge this pair through public HTTP routes so the worker unpickles attacker-staged bytes. This lets an ordinary authenticated inference caller execute arbitrary Python in the worker process, even with insecure serialization disabled.
actions: Check whether your deployments enable the SHM multimodal processor cache.

action_quotes.action: Check whether your deployments enable the SHM multimodal processor cache.
action_quotes.quote: When --mm-processor-cache-type shm is enabled, vLLM's multimodal SHM cache represents a cached item with an address and monotonic_id pair and treats that pair as authority to dereference shared memory in the worker.

who: vLLM deployments using SHM multimodal caching
threats.quote: An ordinary authenticated inference caller can execute arbitrary Python in the worker process on a deployment that uses SHM multimodal caching.

threats.title: vLLM request-controlled processor code revision allows code execution
threats.headline: Untrusted vLLM multimodal requests can swap processor code revision, running arbitrary code on remote-code deployments
threats.summary: Importing a Python module is arbitrary code execution in the vLLM API/renderer process.
actions: Keep trust_remote_code disabled where it is not required.
Put the tokenize endpoint behind authentication.

action_quotes.action: Keep trust_remote_code disabled where it is not required.
action_quotes.quote: The default trust_remote_code=False configuration is not affected.

action_quotes.action: Put the tokenize endpoint behind authentication.
action_quotes.quote: Protect /tokenize with the configured authentication policy as defense in depth.

who: deployments serving multimodal models with dynamic processor code
threats.quote: Importing a Python module is arbitrary code execution in the vLLM API/renderer process.

threats.title: LiteLLM proxy arbitrary local file read via credentials alias
threats.headline: Low-privilege LiteLLM proxy users could read local files, exposing master and provider API keys
threats.summary: Reading environment files can disclose the master key and provider API keys, escalating to full proxy-admin control.
threats.quote: Reading files such as /proc/self/environ can disclose LITELLM_MASTER_KEY and provider API keys, so the impact can escalate to full proxy-admin control.

threats.title: LiteLLM proxy salt key reuse allows admin escalation
threats.headline: LiteLLM internal users could forge admin tokens and run arbitrary commands on the proxy host
threats.summary: An internal user could request an API key with a forged admin credential in its metadata, then present the encrypted result as a bearer token to gain full administrative access. That access includes executing arbitrary commands through the MCP stdio endpoint.
actions: Turn off experimental UI login until patched, accepting that CLI SSO and gateway login break.

action_quotes.action: Turn off experimental UI login until patched, accepting that CLI SSO and gateway login break.
action_quotes.quote: If you cannot upgrade immediately, set EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN=false .

threats.quote: An internal user can escalate to proxy admin and execute arbitrary commands on the host.
